target_geometry.note: THE TARGET IS AN INTERIOR BYTE OF THE BODY, NOT AN INSTRUCTION ENTRY. This is the first fact about this VA and it shapes everything else.
target_geometry.target_byte_role: the MOST significant byte of that instruction's 32-bit absolute-address operand (moffs32)
why_this_is_established_three_ways: The image bytes: a linear decode of the 73 bytes at 0x00e7d2b7 places a 5-byte A1 moffs32 instruction at 0x00e7d2bc and the next instruction at 0x00e7d2c2, so 0x00e7d2c0 is interior. Confirmed by GhidraMCP /read_memory at 0x00e7d2b7, which returns 8d44241c50a1043c6b018d4c242c51..., and independently by objdump over the same bytes read out of the PE at RVA 0xa7d2c0.
The evidence listing: it spells `MOV EAX,[0x016b3c04]` at 0x00e7d2bc and `LEA ECX,[ESP + 0x2c]` at 0x00e7d2c1, agreeing instruction for instruction and address for address with the byte decode.

The xref export: knowledgegraph/triage/xrefs-2540f2ca.tsv carries thirteen call rows whose caller_va is 0x00e7d070 and NONE whose caller_va is 0x00e7d2c0. The export is keyed on the caller's entry point, so a VA with no rows is not an entry point.

reconstructed_span.note: Of a 224-instruction body this package reconstructs ONE basic block: the straight-line fall-through block that contains the target byte. It is the smallest unit the machine evidence fully determines -- single entry, no branch inside it, no callee of its own, single exit.
reconstructed_span.exit: JMP 0x00e7d348, the block's only transfer out
reconstructed_span.length_justification: the twenty-one instruction lengths sum to 0x49 = 73 bytes exactly, with nothing left over and no overlap

observed_original_abi.variadic: UNDECIDED. The record's abstention list includes variadic_not_decidable_from_listing and states that variadic suspicion removes any guarantee about the stack-argument extent. The block's five pushed words are exactly what its own JMP tail consumes -- the shared tail at 0x00e7d348 does `CALL 0x00e394f0` then `ADD ESP,0x14`, and 0x14 is five words -- which is an observation about this block and not a determination of the enclosing function's convention.
observed_original_abi.frame: the body does `SUB ESP,0x30` at 0x00e7d076 and `PUSH EDI` / `PUSH EBP` / `PUSH ESI`, and undoes all of it in its epilogue with `POP ESI` / `POP EBP` / `POP EDI` / `ADD ESP,0x30` / `RET`. EBP is a general register here: there is no `MOV EBP,ESP`, and the record says so (frame.fp false, ebp_is_general_register true).
observed_original_abi.sret: present false per the record's own sub-record; nothing in this block writes through a hidden pointer

observed_mechanics: 0x00e7d2b7  LEA EAX,[ESP + 0x1c] then 0x00e7d2bb PUSH EAX: the first frame address, F+0x1c, with no PUSH yet executed.

0x00e7d2bc  MOV EAX,[0x016b3c04] (bytes a1 04 3c 6b 01): a 5-byte A1 moffs32 load of an absolute word. THE TARGET BYTE 0x00e7d2c0 IS THE TOP BYTE OF THAT OPERAND -- 0x01, the high byte of 0x016b3c04 -- and is not an instruction boundary.
0x00e7d2c1  LEA ECX,[ESP + 0x2c] then 0x00e7d2c5 PUSH ECX: read with one PUSH already done, so the address is F-4+0x2c = F+0x28, NOT F+0x2c.
0x00e7d2c6..0x00e7d2e6  nine consecutive `MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x24 + 4k],ESI`: read with two PUSHes done, so they cover F+0x1c .. F+0x3c inclusive -- nine dwords, 36 bytes, one contiguous region.

ALL THREE frame addresses the block pushes (F+0x1c, F+0x28, F+0x34) point INTO the nine dwords it then overwrites. The addresses are computed first and the overwrite happens afterwards, so the pushed values are unaffected by it and the words at those addresses are not. This is a consequence of the ORDER of the two effects and of no single opcode.
0x00e7d2ea  MOV ECX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x5190]: a 32-bit read 0x5190 bytes into whatever the absolute word held. A four-byte read is claimed; what lives there is not known and is not named.
0x00e7d2f0  LEA EDX,[ESP + 0x3c] then 0x00e7d2f4 PUSH EDX: read with two PUSHes done, so F-8+0x3c = F+0x34.

0x00e7d2f5  ADD ECX,0x10: an adjustment of the loaded VALUE, not a memory displacement. Reported as a distinction here because the validator reads every `+ 0x..` in the span as a declared displacement.

0x00e7d2f9  PUSH 0x9ef61113 then 0x00e7d2fe JMP 0x00e7d348: the block's selector immediate and its only transfer out. The shared tail immediately does CALL 0x00e394f0 and ADD ESP,0x14, so the tail consumes exactly the five words the block pushed.

The store source is the register ESI, which the BLOCK never writes. The listing's only definition of ESI is `XOR ESI,ESI` at 0x00e7d23d, 0x8a bytes before this block's first instruction. That is recorded as a machine observation with its address; whether ESI is provably zero on EVERY path into this block is a dataflow question this package does not settle, so the model takes the stored word as a parameter and is driven with both zero and a sentinel.

The SIBLING ARM: the predicate at 0x00e7d28d..0x00e7d2b5 falls into this block when it holds and into 0x00e7d300 when it does not. That second arm builds the same five-word transfer over the same nine-word region and differs visibly in one thing: its selector immediate is 0xac7161b5 where this block's is 0x9ef61113. Two arms, one selector each, one shared tail. What the selectors MEAN is not established by anything in this repository.

The body's terminator at 0x00e7d360 is the ONE-byte RET (0xc3, read out of the image), with `ADD ESP,0x30` and three POPs before it that undo the body's OWN frame. That is what `cleanup.bytes 0` and `cleanup.side caller` rest on, with the record's evidence string `ret with no immediate`.

confidence.block_transcription: high -- twenty-one lengths consume the 73 bytes exactly, and the independently written table in the model test agrees instruction for instruction

unresolved_questions: What is the word at the absolute address 0x016b3c04, and what object does it point at? The block reads it and then reads 0x5190 bytes into the result, but no type, size, class or lifetime for either is established here and none is guessed.
What do the two selector immediates 0x9ef61113 and 0xac7161b5 mean, and what does the callee at 0x00e394f0 do with them? The two-arm shape is established; the meaning of either arm is not.

Is ESI provably zero on every path that reaches 0x00e7d2b7? The listing has exactly one definition of ESI, `XOR ESI,ESI` at 0x00e7d23d, and it dominates this block by inspection, but no dominator computation was run and the model does not depend on it.
What is the enclosing function FUN_00e7d070 for? Its decompilation was never collected, eleven callees are unresolved, and 203 of its 224 instructions are untranscribed here.

Is this body a virtual member of some class, and of which? The record declines to name a receiver and the body contains no indirect transfer, so nothing in this repository places it in a class or a slot.

Is the enclosing function variadic? The record lists variadic_suspected and variadic_not_decidable_from_listing and states that the suspicion removes any guarantee about the stack-argument extent. The block's own five words are accounted for; the function's are not.

Why does the CALLS oracle see no callee for this VA? The xref export keys rows on 0x00e7d070, the function's real entry, and carries no row for the interior address 0x00e7d2c0, while the evidence pack's listing is the whole 224-instruction body. The two machine oracles therefore disagree by construction for this target and the disagreement is not a property of any reconstruction.

focused_test.note: all eight cells were built and run, not one. The -O0 rows run 287 checks and the -O1/-O2/-O3 rows 289 because case K decodes the compiler's own emitted code and is skipped at -O0, where an unoptimised build is free to fold and materialise the constants differently. Case I's ESP sampler is a real three-instruction function called from C++, and the harness's own terminator forms are decoded at run time before either cell is believed. Three earlier drafts of case I were wrong -- a local's address under a frame pointer, a schedulable inline ESP read, and a sample held in a caller-saved register across a call -- and each is named in the source as the reason the current shape is what it is.

Reaching PASS would require a calling convention the machine record does not state: conventions.calling_convention is null, confidence UNKNOWN, and the one candidate is a candidate list entry, not a determination. This package declares no convention and leaves the WARN standing.
warning_checks.GLOBALS: the complete 224-instruction listing names three data-segment addresses (0x016b3c04, 0x016b3c14, 0x0147b9f0) and the xref export carries no data-reference edge type, so there is nothing to corroborate them against. No source content can change this arm: with data addresses present in the listing, every arm of the check is a WARN.
warning_checks.FIELDS/OFFSETS: the machine-derived receiver record names no receiver register (reason ecx_reassigned_before_deref), so the displacements the source declares have no machine receiver evidence to be grounded in. Note that the validator's own scan also reads this package's C++ struct members -- outcome.tail.fifth and window->byte -- as field declarations; they are named members of two package-local structs and are not claims about any object's layout.

blocking_check.detail: the machine-vs-machine rule: the xref export records 0 callee(s) for 0x00e7d2c0 and the complete 224-instruction listing shows 11 direct transfer(s), and the two sets disagree. The cause is the target's GEOMETRY, not the reconstruction: the export at knowledgegraph/triage/xrefs-2540f2ca.tsv is keyed on a caller's ENTRY POINT and carries thirteen rows for 0x00e7d070 and none for the interior address 0x00e7d2c0, while the evidence pack's disassembly category holds the WHOLE 224-instruction body. The two oracles therefore cannot agree for an interior-address target.
blocking_check.why_no_package_content_can_reach_it: the two ways to make the sets agree are both fabrications: dropping one of the eleven transfers the body demonstrably makes, or naming a callee address in the source that the export cannot reach -- which the validator would report as a source-side refutation, a second and worse failure. Neither is done.
